Phenomena — findings and rebuild

Did studying Grok 4.7 improve the first version?

Top finding: the first Muse Wonder 1.0 version had more real 3D content, but Grok 4.7 looked more photographic in all five still frames, because softness, haze, blur and restrained colour hid its simplicity while hard facets and stylised props exposed the Muse geometry. Every improvement below attacks one of those observed weaknesses, scene by scene. All fifteen frames were captured fresh for this page at 1280×708 from the three running animations.

First comparison — Grok 4.7: 5  ·  Muse Wonder 1.0 (prev): 0   |   Current — Muse Wonder 1.0: 5, each narrowly

Read each row left to right: Grok 4.7, the first Muse version that lost to it, then the current Muse version after the finding in that row was applied. Click any frame to play that animation live in this grid — the first version is hosted on this site under prev/ so all fifteen frames are playable.

The river

Finding: Grok won on a sun-glitter path, warm haze and no hard edges; the first Muse frame had oversaturated teal water, uniform lollipop trees and a faceted black foreground cliff.

Improvement: Reframed at water level into the sun, added depth-of-field and haze, muted the colour grade, and replaced the trees with soft foliage masses kept out of the foreground.

The falls

Finding: Grok won by shooting the falls like a long exposure: streaked water, drifting mist and a faint rainbow. The first Muse waterfall was a flat, bright white rectangle ringed by low-poly rocks and trees.

Improvement: Rebuilt the falls as broken, glassy ribbons with dark lanes between them, shot low and close, with fine spray and a soft foreground so it reads as a long-exposure photograph.

The aurora

Finding: Grok won, its strongest scene: green-violet curtains reflected in dead-still water. The first Muse aurora was a single green band with a hard edge over flat blue snow, with flakes reading as artifacts.

Improvement: Widened the curtains off-frame with a violet crown, put a frozen lake in the foreground, and made that lake a true planar mirror so the treeline and curtains reflect in it.

The eruption

Finding: Grok won on surface detail: its cracked, glowing lava crust looked like a lava-lake photograph. The first Muse flow was a smooth neon tube on a smooth cone, though it had the better composition.

Improvement: Gave the cone a cracked-crust lava shader, a glowing mottled lava river from the crater, rising embers and a backlit dusk framing.

The storm

Finding: Grok won with an open-water seascape: layered black cloud, fine rain streaks, whitecaps and a near-monochrome palette hiding every synthetic cue. The first Muse storm had sparse white rain dots, a flat grey sky and rounded tree props.

Improvement: Moved the storm to open water under dark scud cloud, made the rain slanted streaks visible across the frame, and added a whitecapped foreground.

How to judge it quickly: in each row, check whether the current frame hides its geometry the way the Grok frame does — soft edges, haze, photographic blur, restrained colour, no stylised foreground props. That was the whole lesson of the first comparison, and it is what the rebuilds applied.
